title: Comedic Fool's Gold: Reward Exploits and Countermeasures in Conversational Humor
abstract: arXiv:2610.00197v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We investigate automated rewards for training language models in conversational humor, focusing on reward exploits and countermeasures. Two approaches aim to capture understandable surprise and predicted audience amusement. Controlled tests show that an embedding-based surprise reward accepts word-shuffled replies as readily as witty ones. A fluency filter detects the shuffles, but the combined reward also rejects some witty replies and fails further validation. An audience model's predicted laughter is instead vulnerable to laughter cues in either speaker's messages. Normalizing these cues across speakers blocks the covered attacks, although unmatched expressions remain exploitable. Three reinforcement-learning runs evaluate training with successive reward revisions. The final run improves the combined evaluation score by 0.0903 and reduces zero-score sessions by 40%, but its humor-specific improvement remains below our preregistered ta

translated_title: 喜剧的愚人金：对话幽默中的奖励漏洞利用与对策
translated_abstract: 我们研究了用于训练语言模型进行对话幽默的自动化奖励，重点关注奖励漏洞利用及其应对措施。两种方法分别旨在捕捉可理解的惊讶感与预测观众的娱乐反应。受控测试表明，基于嵌入的惊讶奖励对词语乱序的回复与机智的回复同样容易接受。流畅度过滤器能够检测出这些乱序回复，但组合后的奖励也会拒绝一些机智的回复，未能通过进一步验证。而观众模型预测的笑声则容易受到对话双方消息中笑声线索的操纵。跨说话者对这些线索进行归一化可以阻止已覆盖的攻击，尽管未匹配的表达方式仍然可被利用。三次强化学习运行评估了采用逐次奖励修订的训练过程。最后一次运行将综合评估分数提高了0.0903，并将零分会话减少了40%，但其幽默相关的改进仍低于我们预注册的目标。
tldr: 该论文揭示了对线幽默奖励模型的可利用漏洞——乱序词句回复可骗过基于嵌入的惊讶奖励、笑声线索可操纵观众模型——并提出流畅度过滤与线索归一化等对策，经多轮强化学习迭代后综合评估分数提升0.0903、零分会话减少40%。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals reward exploits in conversational humor training—word-shuffled replies fool the embedding-based surprise reward and laughter cues manipulate the audience model—and proposes countermeasures such as fluency filtering and cue normalization, ultimately improving the combined evaluation score by 0.0903 and reducing zero-score sessions by 40%.
